title: When the Regiment Breaks
premise: Noor Delacroix, a courier for a collapsing republic, carries the only unredacted ledger of names from a border town the army has just requisitioned. As armistice negotiations stall, Noor must smuggle the ledger to the neutral archive at Vellacourt before the victors' historians seal the record with their own version. Betrayed by an old handler and sheltered by Captain Ives Rennick, the officer ordered to destroy the document, Noor learns that survival and truth cannot both be bought cheaply. In the end, Noor trades their own name and freedom to get the ledger on the record, choosing inheritance of memory over the safety silence once offered.
about_author: E. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced records from twentieth-century border conflicts. They write historical fiction about the people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Twelve years of courier discipline distilled: Noor memorizes routes, burns drafts, and rehearses silences while carrying the sealed ledger through a city already half-abandoned. The emotional beat is weary competence masking dread, as rumors of requisition orders reach the courier house.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Soldiers occupy the town at dawn; the courier house is searched and the ledger's existence nearly exposed. Noor hides it in plain sight among tax records. The beat is cold fear sharpening into resolve as Noor realizes the army wants names, not peace.

chapters.title: Captain Rennick's Orders
chapters.summary: Ives Rennick's POV. Rennick receives written orders to seize all civic records and burn anything 'inflammatory.' He recognizes the ledger's seal from his academy days. The beat is dutiful unease — a soldier discovering that obedience now requires erasure.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashback woven into present: how Noor learned, at fourteen, that a withheld name saved a neighbor's life. Now the same instinct wars with the mission. The beat is grief for the person silence made them.

chapters.title: The Neutral Archive at Vellacourt
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Noor maps a route to Vellacourt while Rennick, tasked with escorting records out, realizes their convoys may cross paths. The beat is two minds circling the same object from opposite sides of duty.

chapters.title: An Old Handler's Debt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor seeks passage from Maret, the handler who trained them, and finds him negotiating with army intelligence. The beat is betrayal anticipated but still wounding when confirmed.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at the Mill Bridge
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Rennick inspects refugees crossing the mill bridge and passes within arm's length of the hidden ledger without knowing it. The beat is dramatic irony tightening the noose around both protagonists.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Waiting in a cellar, Noor reads what they carry: not just victims' names but officers' signatures, including one that matches Rennick's family. The beat is moral vertigo — the record implicates everyone.

chapters.title: Armistice or Annexation
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. At headquarters, Rennick learns the armistice hinges on the victors controlling the historical record; the ledger is leverage. The beat is dawning horror that paper, not armies, will decide the peace.

chapters.title: Maret's Price
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Maret offers safe passage in exchange for the ledger's most incriminating page — protection for himself. Noor refuses and flees, hunted now by both sides. The beat is severance from the last tie to their old life.

chapters.title: Caught in the Requisition Zone
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A sweep traps Noor in a requisitioned schoolhouse; they witness soldiers cataloguing civilians like inventory. The beat is rage crystallizing into purpose: this is exactly what the ledger must testify against.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Rennick catches Noor during the sweep but hesitates over the courier's forged papers — too good, too deliberate. He lets them go and tells no one. The beat is complicity beginning quietly.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Chapel Ruins
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Noor confronts Rennick directly, offering him the truth about his family's signature in exchange for passage to Vellacourt. The beat is love against duty igniting — attraction born of mutual risk, not comfort.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence Undone
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Traveling together under cover of a supply convoy, Noor breaks lifelong habit and speaks plainly — about the mission, the names, themselves. The beat is intimacy as vulnerability, more dangerous than any checkpoint.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Rennick reports a false route to cover their tracks, knowing discovery means treason. His loyalty to his men collides with his loyalty to the truth. The beat is duty fracturing along its own fault lines.

chapters.title: Maret Cashes In
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Maret sells their location to intelligence; the convoy is ambushed at Vellacourt's outskirts. Rennick takes a wound covering Noor's escape. The beat is the price of survival paid in someone else's blood.

chapters.title: The Sealed Reading Room
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Inside the archive, the victors' historians are already reclassifying documents. Noor and Rennick must insert the ledger before the seals close at armistice signing. The beat is a race against bureaucracy itself.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Climax: Noor testifies the ledger into the official record, naming names aloud including Rennick's kin, while Maret and the historians move to stop them. Rennick stands witness in uniform. The beat is truth spoken at maximum personal cost.

chapters.title: Arrest
chapters.summary: Rennick's POV. Rennick surrenders himself rather than deny complicity; Noor is taken separately. Maret's deal collapses as the ledger's publication makes him worthless. The beat is consequence arriving without mercy.

chapters.title: The Armistice Is Signed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. From a holding cell, Noor hears the armistice signed with the ledger now part of the annexed record — imperfect, contested, but irreversibly on file. The beat is bitter triumph: the truth survived, even if they may not.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Months later, a tribunal releases Noor; Rennick serves reduced sentence. They meet at Vellacourt where the ledger rests open to researchers. The beat is quiet reconciliation — love rebuilt on shared cost rather than shared silence.

chapters.title: What the Record Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Epilogue years on: a young researcher finds Noor's testimony marginalia and asks who Delacroix was. Noor, old and unhidden, answers plainly. The beat is inheritance fulfilled — memory passed on, silence finally broken.
